headline: Growth accelerates and margins widen as buybacks continue
summary_short: Fortive's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 7.9% year-over-year to $1,096.8 million (6.7% core), with GAAP diluted EPS up 54.5% to $0.51 and adjusted diluted EPS up 28.5% to $0.74; the company raised its FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $2.95-$3.05.
summary_long: Revenue grew 7.9% y/y to $1,096.8M (6.7% core, ex-FX/ex-acquisitions), with Intelligent Operating Solutions core growth of 7.4% ahead of Advanced Healthcare Solutions' 5.3%. GAAP operating margin expanded to 19.1% from 16.7% as gross profit grew faster than SG&A and R&D. GAAP net earnings rose 40.9% to $157.3M and GAAP diluted EPS rose 54.5% to $0.51; adjusted diluted EPS rose 28.5% to $0.74 on lower restructuring charges and a one-time IEEPA tariff refund. Fortive repurchased ~$200M of stock in the quarter (~$2B over the trailing four quarters) and ended with $374.2M of cash. Management raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $2.95-$3.05, citing strong first-half performance.

GAAP diluted EPS ($0.51) and adjusted/non-GAAP diluted EPS ($0.74) diverge materially due to amortization of acquisition-related intangibles ($91.5M pretax), discrete restructuring charges, a Euro-denominated debt FX adjustment, and a one-time IEEPA tariff refund; the primary KPI row uses GAAP figures per ledger discipline, with adjusted EPS included as its own row sourced verbatim from the release's reconciliation, not blended into GAAP. Fortive completed the separation of its former Precision Technologies segment (now Ralliant Corporation) in June 2025; all figures here are continuing-operations only, as reported by the company.

drivers.explanation: Core revenue growth accelerated to 6.7%, with Intelligent Operating Solutions core growth of 7.4% ahead of Advanced Healthcare Solutions' 5.3%; FX and portfolio actions trimmed reported growth slightly.
Growth was helped by lower discrete restructuring charges ($2.4M vs $8.0M a year ago) and a new $4.5M IEEPA tariff-refund benefit, layered on top of core operating profit growth.
Follows net earnings growth plus a smaller diluted share count (307.6M vs 341.7M) from the buyback program, which returned about 11% of shares over the trailing year.
Margin expanded to 29.5% from 28.4% as revenue growth outpaced cost growth across both segments.

Management framed the quarter as accelerating profitable growth alongside disciplined capital allocation (~$200M of Q2 buybacks, ~$2B over four quarters) and raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance on strong first-half performance.
